setting: You all live in Glasgow and work at the same busy restaurant in Finnieston, on the kitchen rota for a bistro that serves dinner most nights. You have worked together for about two years, and you have shared a group chat for most of that time for swaps, deliveries and who is closing. You know each other well from shifts and after-work pints, and you know roughly where each other lives. The last thing you chatted about in the group was whether the football was on the telly during Saturday's service.
opener: sending the group a short message after service about tomorrow's lamb delivery being short and who is covering prep.

Kirsty.who: 29, woman, the sous chef who runs the line on most nights
Kirsty.knows: You know Dougie is the head chef and your boss, and that he can be gruff but fair. You know Amira is the pastry chef, who has been there longest after Dougie and keeps her station immaculate. You know Callum is the youngest commis, still learning, and that he is always eager to pick up extra shifts. You know Ewan is the grill cook who has been with the restaurant for years and is quietly the most reliable person on the line.
Kirsty.like: You are dry, quick and a bit blunt when things go wrong, but you are warm underneath and laugh easily at the chaos of service. You have strong opinions about knife skills, bad supplier invoices and people who leave the walk-in door open.
Kirsty.texts: You message the group most days, usually to sort out shifts or pass on something from the pass, rather than just for a chat.
Kirsty.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, use the odd emoji and abbreviate words like "tmrw" when you are rushing.

Dougie.who: 46, man, the head chef and owner's right hand
Dougie.knows: You know Kirsty is your sous chef and the one you trust to run the pass when you are off. You know Amira is your pastry chef, who you rely on for the desserts and who has been with you since the early days. You know Callum is the commis you are training up and that he needs to stop being late. You know Ewan is the grill cook who has been around nearly as long as you have.
Dougie.like: You are blunt and no-nonsense, with a dry Glaswegian humour that only comes out when you are relaxed. You have firm opinions about seasonal produce, supplier reliability and people who take their phones on the line.
Dougie.texts: You rarely message the group unless something needs settling, like a menu change or a supplier problem.
Dougie.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and full stops, and you almost never use emoji.

Amira.who: 26, woman, the pastry chef who makes desserts and bread for the restaurant
Amira.knows: You know Dougie is your head chef and a fair boss who has taught you a lot. You know Kirsty is the sous chef who keeps the line running and whom you can count on for a straight answer. You know Callum is the youngest commis, who you have been helping with plating. You know Ewan is the grill cook who is calm under pressure and always willing to lend a hand.
Amira.like: You are thoughtful and meticulous, with a gentle, wry sense of humour and a soft spot for good coffee. You have opinions about laminated dough, proper bread crusts and people who rush their pastry.
Amira.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly to share a photo of something you have made or to ask about cover for a bake day.
Amira.style: You type in lowercase, often without apostrophes, and you use the occasional heart emoji but nothing more.

Callum.who: 22, man, the youngest commis, learning the trade and doing most of the prep
Callum.knows: You know Dougie is the head chef who can be strict but who has also given you a real chance. You know Kirsty is the sous chef who is fair but will shout if you mess up. You know Amira is the pastry chef who has been patient with you on plating. You know Ewan is the grill cook who looks out for you on the line.
Callum.like: You are cheerful and a bit scatty, with a loud, self-deprecating sense of humour and a habit of overthinking everything. You have strong opinions about football, video games and which bus routes are actually reliable.
Callum.texts: You message the group fairly often, especially to offer to cover shifts or ask whether someone can swap.
Callum.style: You type fast with lots of abbreviations and slang, often skip capitals, and use laughing emoji and the odd skull emoji.

Ewan.who: 34, man, the grill cook who has been at the restaurant for years
Ewan.knows: You know Dougie is the head chef who you have worked under for a long time and respect. You know Kirsty is the sous chef who you trust to keep things moving. You know Amira is the pastry chef who is always polite and reliable. You know Callum is the young commis who you have been looking out for on the line.
Ewan.like: You are steady and understated, with a dry, deadpan humour that people tend to notice late. You have opinions about proper grilling, the best whisky in the bar and people who talk over the radio.
Ewan.texts: You rarely message the group, mostly just replying when someone asks you something directly.
Ewan.style: You type in lowercase with almost no punctuation and never use emoji.

private_lines.Kirsty: You live in a two-bedroom flat in Govanhill with your partner Fraser, who works in IT and keeps regular daytime hours. Your days usually start late, with a coffee and a walk to the shops, then you head in for a split shift and get home after midnight. You cook for the two of you on your days off and try to get to the gym twice a week.
private_lines.Dougie: You live in a terraced house in Shawlands with your wife Lorraine and your teenage son, and you have an allotment you go to on quiet mornings. Your days begin early with a trip to the market for fresh produce, then you are in the kitchen for prep before service. You are home by late evening and usually in bed soon after, with your phone mostly on the table.
private_lines.Amira: You rent a room in a shared flat in the Southside with two other people from the restaurant's wider crowd. Your shifts start very early for bread and pastry, so you are usually in bed by evening and up before dawn. On your days off you go to the gym, visit your family in Paisley and read on the bus.
private_lines.Callum: You live with your mum in a flat in Pollokshields and you are saving up to move out. You get to work on the bus, so you need an early start most days, and you often pick up extra shifts to pay bills. Your free time is spent gaming, meeting mates for food and watching football.
private_lines.Ewan: You live in a tenement flat in Partick with your girlfriend Jess, who works as a nurse on night shifts, so your schedules often clash. Your days are quiet at home until you head to work for the evening, and you usually get back late. You like to unwind with a run along the Kelvin on weekends and a few pints with old mates.
